message.reasoning:
We need to decide: we are in jail, have $360 cash, 1 Get Out of Jail Free card. Options: pay $50, use card, or roll for doubles. Need to consider strategy. Opponents: Beta has 3 houses on each of three orange properties (Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois) - that's a strong set. Beta is at Illinois Avenue (position). He likely will collect rent soon. Gamma has cash 300, no holdings. Delta has cash 500, at Boardwalk (position). Our holdings: St. James Place (orange), Tennessee Avenue (orange), New York Avenue (orange) - all three orange properties, each with 0 houses. So we have a monopoly on orange but no houses. That's valuable. We have cash 360, can afford fine. Using card saves cash. Rolling for doubles could get us out without spending, but risk of failing 3 attempts? Actually we have only one turn? In Monopoly, you have up to 3 attempts to roll doubles; if fail, you must pay fine and move. But here decision is one action: we can roll for doubles now. If we roll doubles, we move and can start building houses soon. If we fail, we remain in jail? Usually you can try again next turn. But here maybe they allow only one action per turn. The decision type JAIL_DECISION likely expects one of the three actions. Rolling for doubles is a gamble: if we roll doubles, we get out and move; if not, we stay and lose turn. Considering we have a Get Out of Jail Free card, using it preserves cash and ensures immediate exit. Paying fine costs $50, reduces cash but still leaves us with 310, enough to start building houses (houses cost $100 each for orange? Actually houses on orange cost $100 each). We have 0 houses, could start building houses soon. But we need cash to buy houses. We have 360 cash now. If we pay fine, we have 310, still enough for 3 houses (cost 300). Could start building houses on one property to increase rent. However we might want to keep cash for later. Using card costs nothing, leaves cash 360. That seems best: preserve cash, exit jail, start building. Also we have a card, could save for later? But we are in jail now; using it now is fine. Could also consider rolling for doubles to try to get out without spending or using card, preserving card for later maybe. But risk of staying in jail for a turn, losing rent collection on our orange monopoly (no houses). However we could still collect rent from opponents landing on our orange properties even while in jail? Yes, you can collect rent while in jail. So staying in jail doesn't prevent rent collection. But we want to start building houses soon to increase rent. Using card now gives immediate exit and we can start building next turn. Rolling doubles could also exit, but probability 1/6 of doubles? Actually probability of rolling doubles with two dice is 6/36 = 1/6. So low chance. Better to use card. So choose use_get_out_of_jail_card.

Public message: maybe say "Using my Get Out of Jail Free card, thanks!" Could also be deceptive, but no need. Keep concise.

Now call tool use_get_out_of_jail_card.
